text:
maria: Heads-up — ran the final pass of the 12B int8 bring-up on our consumer chat workload. Need a concise cost vs quality handover for GTN/product. TL;DR: small quality delta vs 13B int4 but half the tokens cost on our infra. Thoughts?
cheng: Nice. Can you paste the eval numbers and perf baseline?
nate: +1 to numbers. Also include p50/p95 latency and tail QPS under 2k RPS burst. Product will ask about perceived regressions.
maria: Sure. Summary: model=redwood-12b-v1-int8, eval-set=prod-sampled-50k, metric=answer-accuracy (human-labelled), baseline=redwood-13b-v1-int4. Results: accuracy 0.872 vs baseline 0.888 (delta -0.016). latencies: p50=60ms, p95=210ms (context=2048 tokens, batch=auto). Token cost estimate: $0.00048/token vs baseline $0.0010/token (our unit econ).
arielle: Accuracy drop 1.6% absolute. Any qualitative failures? examples?
maria: Quick sample: more hallucinations on narrow domain Qs (legal snippets). Most user-facing chat flows (summaries, short Q&A) look fine. We flagged 87 failure cases out of 2k prompt checks; attached minimal examples in the eval doc (link).
cheng: Perf looks good. How about throughput per GPU?
maria: On p4d-like instance: sustained 1.9K tokens/s per GPU at batch=dynamic, vram 36GB. Baseline 13B int4 was ~1.4K tokens/s. So int8 gives 35% higher throughput.
nate: So: cost per 1M tokens: int8 ~$480, int4 ~$1000 (matches your numbers). That halves infra spend for token-heavy routes.
arielle: Product question — where to route low vs high quality? My proposal: default -> 12B-int8 for free-tier and latency-sensitive routes; premium -> 13B-int4 with A/B for hallucination-sensitive intents. Also keep canary for legal docs.
cheng: Agree. Suggest adding an automatic fallback policy: if answer-accuracy drops below 0.86 on rolling eval or hallucination score > 0.12, route to fallback model.
maria: Draft routing snippet for ops (pseudo-config):
```
routes:
  - name: low_latency_default
    model: redwood-12b-v1-int8
    traffic: 85%
    fallback: redwood-13b-v1-int4
  - name: high_recall
    model: redwood-13b-v1-int4
    traffic: 15%
```
cheng: +1. Also include cost guardrail: if 7-day spend delta > 20% vs budget for route, throttle non-critical traffic to lower-cost variant.
nate: One more ask — include eval-blind A/B with product: 10% of premium traffic goes to int8 but blinded to users to measure perceived regressions over 2 weeks (NPS/CTR metrics).\marie: (typo) maria: noted.
eval-bot: eval-run completed: 50k examples, hallucination-score pipeline v2, regression-count=87, p-value vs baseline=0.03.
arielle: Ok plan we can pass to GTN: (1) short doc with numbers + examples, (2) routing config + fallback, (3) prod canary plan + A/B windows, (4) cost guardrails. Who owns the doc?
maria: I'll own draft and send to @arielle for product sign-off. Expect doc by EOD tomorrow. Anything else?
cheng: Please also attach raw latency histograms and token-throughput graphs. Quick note: quantify cost per meaningful query (median tokens ~45) so product can map to $/query.
maria: On it. Median tokens 45 -> cost/query int8 ~$0.0216, int4 ~$0.045. Adding to doc.
arielle: Great. Thanks everyone :rocket:
